headline: Leafs update injury status of Tanev, Tavares, Domi, Joshua
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that several of Toronto's injured regulars are getting closer to returning, with the outlet posting updates on the status of Chris Tanev, John Tavares, Max Domi and Dakota Joshua. The headline and summary don't say who is closest or give any return dates.

The returns matter because Toronto's 7-4-2 record looks better than its play. Expected goals measures the quality of chances taken and allowed, and the Leafs have 47.6 percent of it so far this season, which means opponents have had slightly better looks. At five-on-five that slips to 45 percent. They've scored 8.7 more goals than their chances would predict, and goalies have saved 5.5 more than expected, a pair of cushions that tend to shrink over time. So a healthier lineup is less a bonus than a need: if it lifts the underlying numbers, the standings position becomes easier to trust. The special teams are steady, with the power play generating 0.74 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing the same.
